questionText: Which Articles in the Constitution of India deal with the Fundamental Rights to "freedom of religion"?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Framing the Constitution.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Framing the Constitution (The Making of the Constitution (Framing the Constitution)):
Part III of the Indian Constitution enshrines Fundamental Rights:
- Articles 14–18: Right to Equality
- Articles 19–22: Right to Freedom
- Articles 23–24: Right against Exploitation
- Articles 25–28: Right to Freedom of Religion (freedom of conscience, management of religious affairs, freedom from taxation for religious promotion, freedom from attendance at religious instruction)
- Articles 29–30: Cultural and Educational Rights of minorities.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

I. First inaugural sitting of the Constituent Assembly
II. Jawaharlal Nehru moves the Objectives Resolution
III. Constituent Assembly formally adopts and enacts the Constitution
IV. The Constitution of India comes into full legal force
(A) I
(B) II
(C) III
(D) IV

Choose the correct chronological sequence from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. Chronology: First sitting (9 Dec 1946) -> Objectives Resolution (13 Dec 1946) -> Constitution adopted (26 Nov 1949) -> Full enforcement (26 Jan 1950).
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (B) is correct.
